imply: To get a point across without putting it into words.
assume: To take something as true without testing it first.
acknowledge: To admit a fact, or signal you noticed someone.
dismiss: To brush an idea aside as not worth your time.
insist: To keep saying something firmly despite objection.
vague: Too unclear or general to be much use.
plausible: Believable enough to accept, though unproven.
presumably: Used when something is likely, judging by what you know.
arguably: Used for a claim you could defend if challenged.
roughly: About that amount, without being exact.
reluctant: Holding back because you would rather not do it.
blunt: Saying it straight, with no effort to soften it.
earnest: Wholly sincere and serious, never joking about it.
defensive: Quick to guard yourself when criticised, often sharply.
stubborn: Holding to your view even after being proven wrong.
outcome: What a process, event, or decision finally produces.
consequence: An event that follows on as a result of an earlier act.
trigger: To set a process in motion, often quite suddenly.
contribute: To be one of the causes, or to give what you can.
stem: To have its origin in a particular cause.
slight: Small enough in size or degree to matter little.
considerable: Large enough in degree to be worth noting.
moderate: Kept within sensible limits, neither big nor small.
excessive: Going well beyond what is needed or proper.
minimal: The least amount there could reasonably be.
occasionally: Now and then, without any regular pattern.
eventually: At last, once the delays are finally over.
meanwhile: While the other thing is still going on.
previously: Earlier on, before the point being discussed.
gradually: In small steps spread over a period of time.
aware: Having noticed that something is going on.
convinced: Fully certain of something, short of hard proof.
skeptical: Inclined to doubt that a claim will really hold up.
indifferent: Uninterested, and untroubled by the outcome.
overwhelmed: Unable to cope with how much has piled up.
nevertheless: All the same, despite the point just made.
whereas: Used to set two things side by side in contrast.
despite: Used when something happens anyway, against expectation.
regardless: Not affected by the facts or problems just raised.
albeit: Though; used to add a brief remark that limits the point.
thorough: Done fully and with care, missing nothing.
sloppy: Done with so little care that the result is messy.
decent: Acceptable enough, if short of impressive.
questionable: Doubtful enough that you would not trust it.
remarkable: Striking enough that people notice and mention it.
agenda: The list of points planned for discussion at a meeting.
deadline: The last possible date by which work must be finished.
delegate: To hand part of your work or authority to another.
workload: How much a person or team must get through.
priority: Whatever you put first and handle before the rest.
compromise: A deal where both sides give up part of their aim.
dispute: A long-running quarrel between people or groups.
negotiate: To talk terms formally until the two sides reach a deal.
concede: To grant that a point is right, even if unwillingly.
settle: To close a quarrel by reaching a final decision.
risky: Carrying a real chance of loss or failure.
uncertain: Not known or settled, and not felt with confidence.
precaution: A step taken ahead of time to prevent trouble.
threat: A person or situation that could cause serious harm.
vulnerable: Open to harm or attack because of a weak point.
shift: A move in position, view, or how a thing is done.
adjust: To make a small change so a thing fits or works better.
adapt: To alter yourself or a thing to suit new conditions.
transform: To change a thing utterly, usually for the better.
decline: To fall away in size, strength, or number over time.
struggle: To strain at something you find very hard.
obstacle: Something in your path that makes progress harder.
setback: A problem that pushes progress back a stage.
cope: To handle a hard situation well enough to carry on.
overcome: To get past a problem so it stops blocking you.
impact: The forceful effect one thing has on another.
undermine: To quietly erode something's strength or standing.
reinforce: To make an idea or structure stronger still.
weaken: To lose strength, or to sap it from something.
boost: To raise an amount or lift a feeling quickly.
frank: Open in speech, even when it is unwelcome news.
tactful: Skilled at raising hard topics without hurting.
harsh: Severe or unkind beyond what the case warrants.
sincere: Genuinely meaning what you say, with no pretence.
sarcastic: Saying the reverse of your meaning in order to mock.
evidence: Facts or signs pointing to what is true.
claim: To assert something as true, as yet unproven.
contradict: To state the reverse of what another said.
justify: To show with good reasons that an act was right.
bias: A slant that keeps judgement from being even.
estimate: To judge a figure roughly, lacking exact data.
accurate: Right in every detail, with no errors at all.
misleading: Creating a false impression while staying literally true.
reliable: Trustworthy because it behaves the same each time.
benchmark: A reference result others are measured against.
budget: A plan setting out how much money can be spent over a period.
expense: Money that has to be paid out, often as a regular cost.
invest: To put money or effort into something, expecting a later gain.
worthwhile: Useful enough to repay the time and effort it costs.
afford: To have the money or the time that something takes.
ambitious: Driven to succeed, and willing to work hard to get there.
humble: Not treating yourself as better than other people.
arrogant: Behaving as though you outrank everyone around you.
generous: Ready to give more help or money than expected.
reserved: Quiet by nature, keeping private matters private.
procedure: The set order of steps a task is normally done in.
stage: One distinct part of a process, before or after others.
implement: To put a plan into action so that it actually works.
monitor: To check on something regularly to see how it changes.
review: To look over something again to judge or amend it.
identify: To work out exactly what something is or where it lies.
address: To start dealing with a problem instead of ignoring it.
resolve: To bring an argument or difficulty to a clean end.
tackle: To set about something difficult with real effort.
prevent: To stop something bad before it has a chance to happen.
perceive: To become aware of something, or read it a certain way.
overlook: To fail to notice something that actually mattered.
distinguish: To tell two or more things apart from each other.
grasp: To take in an idea fully, even a difficult one.
misinterpret: To take a meaning in entirely the wrong way.
flexible: Able to bend, or to shift with new conditions.
rigid: Stiff, unbending, and set against change.
fragile: Breaking easily, so it needs careful handling.
durable: Built to last a long time without wearing out.
versatile: Good for many uses, or skilled at many things.
rely: To lean on someone or something to come through.
appreciate: To feel thankful for a thing, or see its worth.
resent: To feel bitter about something you find unfair.
betray: To break the trust of someone who counted on you.
tolerate: To put up with something unpleasant without protest.
anticipate: To expect something and get ready for it in advance.
predict: To state what you believe the future will hold.
speculate: To guess about something without the facts to be sure.
inevitable: Bound to happen, with no way at all to stop it.
unlikely: Probably not true, or probably not going to occur.
flaw: A fault or weak point that keeps a thing from perfect.
drawback: A downside to something that is otherwise good or useful.
merit: A good quality in something that earns praise.
shortcoming: A fault that leaves a person or a system less able.
virtue: A fine moral trait, such as honesty or patience.
intense: Extreme in strength, force, or the feeling involved.
mild: Gentle in degree, causing little trouble or pain.
severe: Extremely bad or serious, often doing real harm.
subtle: Faint enough to be missed, yet still carrying weight.
drastic: Extreme and sudden, taken when matters are urgent.
accountable: Obliged to answer for your actions and their results.
blame: To name someone as the cause of a bad outcome.
obligation: Something a law, promise, or duty makes you do.
entitled: Acting as if owed special treatment you never earned.
liable: Legally on the hook for damage, loss, or injury caused.
conclude: To settle on what is true after weighing up the facts.
determine: To establish a fact exactly, or to fix what the result is.
hesitate: To pause before acting because you feel unsure.
commit: To pledge your time or effort firmly to something.
abandon: To leave a person, place, or plan behind for good.
